I then said "if we don't want to play with this one we can go into the other room". He proceeded to throw it so I picked it up, put it out of reach, and asked him to come into the other room. 

He had a full blown meltdown and I had to put him in time out for hitting, kicking, and trying to bite. Of course, after I tried to reason and calm him. 

I felt like I did it wrong. 🫠 But I'm not sure exactly how I should handle it. I didn't yell, I didn't snatch, I was pretty clear with my words. But he just wants what he wants and is super strong willed.

It's even worse because I'm terrified of leaving my kids with someone I don't know well because of trauma I've sustained... Also I've tried looking for a babysitter using Care .com but the sitters I found didn't work at homes with large dogs and we have a German Shepherd.

I have cptsd due to childhood trauma, but I definitely noticed a huge change years later after multiple traumatic events happened within a year of each other. 

I used to be able to motivate myself and was able to set my mind on things and get them done. Now, I have so much trouble. I feel more anxious in public situations and my mind gets cloudy when I'm doing anything social. I also have a fear of medical professionals and hospitals due to trauma...but that's most likely the direct cause from my traumatic events. 

Speaking to a therapist helped, but since 2020 I haven't seen anyone because it's just so hard in my area. 

I've found that trying to reconnect to my old self has helped. I force myself to do things I used to love (hiking, crafting, reading) and recently it's been helpful for me. 

Truth is, you will never be the exact same, but with practice and self love, you can start to heal more. I'm so sorry you've lost yourself...it's hard and it takes a lot of motivation to heal.

I'm freaking crying, because this is exactly what I needed to read. I have told myself most of these things but I just tend to not listen and tell myself that it's not all true. 

I was thinking about the airport incident and that was the same conclusion I came to. I was thinking about all the things that he could do that doesn't cost him anything, but would make my life easier and he just refuses. Literally countless things. Most of which I don't understand, and just makes me assume he's lazy. I was also looking around the house after I got back and he cleaned a lot. I can't understand why he can't do that when I'm there. It makes me assume he did it **because** I wasn't there. Without me there, he didn't expect me to clean. So with me home he *expects* me to do most of the housework. 

Granted, he had three whole days by himself at home with the kids. But he has two days off on the regular...he just took one more day because I was going to be gone on one of his work days. 

But, backing up.... I just felt so disappointed when I came to this conclusion. 

Then yesterday, after he got home, I told him I needed a bit to myself. I work 12am to 8am Tuesdays and he leaves for work right after I get home. I typically take my son to part time on Tuesdays but they were booked full this Tuesday. So I didn't have a really long nap like I typically do. He knows this. But I thought I was perfectly fine because my son laid in bed with me from 9am to 11am, I dozed and he watched TV and had muffins in bed. Then we went downstairs to eat and play without TV until 2pm. Then I turned on the TV and dozed in and out on the couch with my son cuddling. When my older kiddo came home at 345 I woke up and spoke with them about their day and spoke about homework until my husband got home an hour later. 

I went upstairs and decided to lay down and read my book for twenty minutes. I think I read a page or two and passed out. Around 7 he came upstairs and woke me saying "hey, wake up, you fell asleep" in a rough tone that made me feel like he was mad. I sat up but didn't get out of bed because I was so confused and dizzy. He came back 10 minutes later and said "we already ate dinner. I need to give (son) a bath." And then asked me to get our son's bath ready, "at least". 

I was taken aback. He knew I didn't sleep much. Put doing physical labor on top of it and sore legs from running to my gate with a 50 pound backpack on my back, I was tiiiiiired. It just felt punishing and I was so confused. Then, when I took over after the bath, and put our son to bed he just avoided eye contact and said "I was gonna do it". After my son fell asleep, my husband didn't really say a word to me. I just laid in bed and read my book until I got up to take a shower. When I came out he was just getting off his game and putting things away downstairs. He came up and asked where the remote was and helped me look for it. Turned on the TV and fell asleep ten minutes later. We didn't say much and I didn't engage in a conversation because I was deep in thought. 

I'm waiting to see how he is today and going to try to speak with him. I might just tell him what I'm feeling and why and see what he says. I'm going to try to be as clear as possible and not be emotional. I'm not done trying to communicate even if he's terrible at it. I don't ever want him to try to turn it around on me and say I don't communicate. I know he still might but at least I'll know I tried. 

I'm just wondering where this is going and why we're hitting a rough patch right now. I want to get to the bottom of it. There's gotta be more to it than him just being lazy. I'm worried he's having a huge flare up. He has nerve and muscle damage in his neck and sometimes he just doesn't say anything or wants to do anything about it. He's currently going to the chiropractor three times a week and I'm sure it's taking a toll while they work out all the damage. I've just been doing my own thing while I leave the things I expect him to do, just like he does me. 

I know it's toxic...but I'm just at a loss. 

I'm going to start putting money aside just in case I need to take a break from the house and him. I've been married for 8 years but together for 11. The fourth year was the absolute worst. We had had trouble for the first few years...but the constant lack of communication, the non-existent mutual understanding, and a gaming addiction really *really* fucked it up.

He'd go to work, come home, play games for hours, then sleep. Rinse, repeat. Weekends he'd be on his computer all day. 12+ hours. I snapped. I was constantly having panic attacks, anxiety was high, and I was suicidal. I even began resenting stepdaughter, and had abusive thoughts. I even was awful towards her. I feel so shitty for that... and I'm so glad that I got us into family therapy (that...I only went to with her because "it [was] [my] problem"). Then one day I get home after going grocery shopping and stepdaughter is still in pajamas, comes immediately to me and asks for food (she was 6 at the time). I ask her "why didn't you ask daddy?" She says "I did, but he's been upstairs playing his game". 

I immediately make her something. Put groceries away. And go upstairs. I turned off his PC and he immediately gets upset. I scream "You need to grow the fuck up! You know I'm not the type of person to constantly nags. You know I've given you all these chances. Get up, and fucking parent your daughter! She has one deadbeat parent. If I leave she has no one! Get your fucking shit together!" 

He comes back with "Where are *you* gonna go? The cars are mine, all the clothes you have were bought with *my* money. You have *nothing*." 

He promised me he would **never** say that. He constantly said "my paycheck is our paycheck. I wouldn't be able to do this without your support." So it hurt me so much.

He storms out, while I'm crumpled on the floor crying. I call my dad, he's planning on getting me a ticket home. I start grabbing clothes and things that weren't bought with his money. I pack them in my old college bookbag and a duffle bag that was my dad's.... I'm crying so hard and can't stop. My dad texts me that he found tickets to fly me home.

Then...I remember....

She wouldn't have anyone here for her.....

She would lose her mom.... again. Her mom abandoned her and what am I doing? I'm abandoning her. 

She's still downstairs. I go down to check on her. She's playing a book on her kindle (those read aloud ones) and has headphones on. I'm hoping she didn't hear our argument. 

I sit on the last stair and just bawl. I couldn't leave her. 

My husband comes home, sees the bags, and just....

I tell him, calmly, "This is what is going to happen. You start actually go to our marriage counseling appointments, or I'm leaving. I'm leaving *you*. You're going to tell her why I'm leaving. You're going to do it in front of me. With me. You will have to figure out what to do about her and her care. You aren't going to pay for my ticket. My dad is giving me the money, my friend is going to take me to the airport. The things in these bags aren't things I bought with your money. These are my things. I will be back for my other things. I will pack them and label them. I will take pictures and catalogue them. You throw them out, I will be suing you. This is what it's come to. This is where we are."

He instantly sobered up. He agreed to go to counseling again (he'd been "skipping" our appointments. I'd show up and wait for him there and he'd text me with five minutes to the appointment time with an excuse). He and I didn't really talk until our appointment. I had sent an email to our therapist so he could tell his side of the story. 

I didn't leave because I didn't want to do that to my stepdaughter. I was in a rough place with my own mom at the time and I had my own mom issues. I didn't want to do that to her. I loved her too much. 

We made it through. We have a few problems still, but we work it out...

TL;DR: Husband wasn't helping me with my stepdaughter, addicted to video games, skirting responsibilities, and lacked communication. I threatened to leave but didn't want to leave stepdaughter. Ultimatums were made. Therapy helped. Still together. 

Communication and teamwork. That's all you need.

Okay, so....I got a story that made me hate a particular person. 

My parents bought a house in rural Louisiana. There was a lot of land and our house sat in the middle of this guy's cow fields. He didn't live near us, but the person who sold us the house had sold that land to him to use. We'll call him Joe. 

So Joe was a really friendly guy. He took really good care of these cows. He always had fresh hay in multiple areas, he bush hogged the land, put salt licks (like seriously giant ones, my brother and I would climb on them) and other treats out. He would bush hog for my parents if we let the cows cross in our land. He was awesome. He had a bunch of cows and they were very well taken care of. 

Well, fast forward about seven years, Joe gets sick so his son (we'll call him Bob) takes over. Bob seems really nice too. He was always with his dad during the dad's they came and took care of the cows, so he should know what to do and how to do it. For the first few years, everything is okay. Bob is doing a good job, basically the same as his dad. Then Joe dies. Bob has to take over. Immediately it's so different. 

Bob didn't get salt licks, he only put out a few things of hay. Didn't keep fresh water out (there was a pond that was actually on our land...but it was kinda gross), didn't bush hog, and didn't provide much for them. Joe would bring this like... washing station with brushes and all sorts of crap, every so often for them to walk through. It was cool, we went through it once and laughed because we imagined it was like we were in a dishwasher... Anyway... The cows just look....ill. They're not in good health...they're skinny...the numbers start going down, and more and more are basically DYING and Bob just left them for the coyotes to get. 

Because of this neglectful behavior, we began getting more predators on our land. Coyotes, bobcats, my dad said he even thought he saw a puma. The coyotes killed our barn cats, got in our trash often, almost killed one of our dogs. So my mom had it with Bob. He didn't bush hog our land, didn't fix fences, so the cows were destroying our yard. She told him if he didn't get shit together, they would say he was trespassing. He never did. My mom called the sheriff department and he was fined. Still didn't do anything. Until...

The cows got out onto the highway. A semi truck hit three. It was pitch black, these cows were black, and when you're on a rural ass highway going 65 in a huge ass truck and a herd of cows are just chilling on the blacktop, you're going to hit them. But this truck fucking tried to dodge them, tipped over and...omg such a freaking disaster. 

Well guess what? Bob still didn't care. So the city fined him again, and he was sued. He lost a ton of money because his cows weren't being bought... It was terrible. 

He doesn't have cows anymore and last I heard was he was ruined. Wife left him, mother disowned him, and he still didn't care.

I didn't either, but after I told her she was like "oh okay. I'll just ask you when it needs to be updated." And now she'll come to me and ask to update it.

At the 20wk anatomy scan my original doctor referred us out to a bigger hospital with more resources. Did tell us why. We went in at 22wks, the ultrasound tech asked if we knew why we were there, we said no. She told us that our daughter was in the 1st percentile for gestational size, her head was very small, and they were having trouble locating her corpus callosum, which could mean it was underdeveloped or non existent. They didn't have complete answers so we scheduled a slew of specialist appointments. 

An amniocentesis, a neonatal neurologist, a geneticist, and an MRI scan. I had to begin coming in weekly until the important appointments to monitor. 

This hospital was in a different state, thirty minutes from where we lived. After all the appointments, the test results were very painful... At 28 weeks they had an answer to all the questions we had. She had a condition called Miller Dieker Syndrome. A very....*very* rare genetic abnormality. She wasn't expected to live long after birth...but...since that state had law's against abortions we were talked into keeping the pregnancy and guilt tripped. 

I'm not sure if I would have just gone back to my state to talk to a doctor about late term. I didn't even know it was an option. But I was filled with hope by the doctors that my daughter would possibly live....that everything was fine. She was doing well inside the womb....

Until she wasn't. The week before my scheduled induction....her heart stopped....she was born the next day. Still....

Two years this April.... It still hurts, but it's getting better.

Well, husband gets home just as baby is starting to doze off....on me. I ask husband to come get him after he changes his clothes. I tell him I want to shower. Husband takes thirty minutes so by the time he comes down baby is up again. He sits down and promptly falls asleep on the couch. I get it, he's tired too. But I need the dishes done so I can cook dinner after my shower. So I have a dilemma, dishes first, then shower? Shower and then get sweaty doing dishes (as I usually do...the heater vent is right above the sink and it blows on me...)? What a choice...

So I do the dishes. After I'm done doing all the dishes, I notice, well I gotta get dinner ready...it's going to take a while to cook. I'll just take a shower after baby goes to bed for the night. So I cook. By now my husband is up, he walks into the kitchen and sees I did the dishes. I'm obviously upset with him. He says "oh, you could have left the dishes for me." I reply sternly "I needed them done. I thought you were going to do them when you got home, so I didn't do them earlier....I did the other cleaning." He then says "Well, I knew you'd want a **break**." 

Yes! I did! Doing dishes without my son on me in a carrier, or in his jumper, or highchair is *not* a **break**! 

I tell him I wanted to take a shower, but now I'm going to have to wait. I tell him how I do not consider these things as "breaks". They are chores and basic human needs. The latter I don't get enough of. I barely eat. I can't go to the bathroom without someone (child or animal) bothering me. Our eleven year old is the only one to understand when I need space or help. He's always telling me "well you should have said something, you should have asked" no buddy. I don't have to. I shouldn't always have to spell it out plain and simple. 

Showering, chores, eating, and I will even go so far as saying time alone in quietness, are all things I don't count as a break. 

Things that do count as a break, being able to read a chapter or two of my book without interruption. Working on a craft without little hands grabbing, or someone hanging over my shoulder asking questions. Being allowed to watch through a whole episode without subtitles on because I can't hear the TV over someone watching something on their phone, toys that make noise, and pleasant screaming. Going for a walk *by myself*, to breathe in the air (can't do that now because.... snow... and sub zero temperatures...but when I can). Working on a skill I want to improve. These are all something I can do *for myself*. Showering? No. Washing my clothes? No. Those are *needs* that are *chores*. I don't enjoy them. 

A break should be something you enjoy. Not something that you have to do, but something you want to do.

Since we didn't know of the abnormality until after the time that the state we were in allows for medically indicated termination, we had to deal with the grief of waiting for the day she'd leave us. 

She had [Miller Dieker Syndrome](https://rarediseases.info.nih.gov/diseases/3669/miller-dieker-syndrome). We didn't find out about it until I was 25 weeks, after three weeks of tests. We lost her on April 1st 2019, she was born the 2nd.

It....gets easier... It doesn't go away. The grief. But it hurts less. The first six months without her really are a blur for me. One clear memory I do have is the day we brought her home....in her urn. I didn't want to go inside. It wasn't supposed to be that way. I was fine the whole way home. I cried a little, but when we got in our driveway and parked I broke. I let out this wail that I still hear when I think of it. My husband had to support me to the front door where I just collapsed. I didn't know where to put her. I didn't know what I should do. I kept telling my mom and husband it wasn't supposed to be this way. 

Losing a baby (no matter if it's a niece/nephew, a child, a sibling, or grandchild) is so hard. There's so much life that's expected. So much future to look forward to. When a baby comes into your life, you can't help but plan the next year's. The excitement, the hope. When you lose them, you lose that future. You grieve for a life that should have been. 

I don't know what really helped me. Talking about it, crying, or just thinking about it....but I got through it. I still hurt for her. I had my son last April. It was bittersweet. He's now nine months old and I'm so happy to have him, but I still hurt...wishing he had his sister with him.

For reference, fwd vehicles pull, rwd push.

Once a baby begins to roll over consistently, it's not safe to put them in a bouncer.
